title: Microsoft Teams: live captions profanity filter now off by default
summary: The briefing matches the roadmap and gives a documented live-captions policy path and PowerShell command without presenting them as profanity-filter controls. Minor corrections should clarify the wording about central control and acknowledge additional conflicting Microsoft documentation on masking, mobile government availability and the transcript policy.

claims.claim: The pages read leave central administrator control of the captions profanity preference unresolved.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Teams profanity filtering live captions centrally administrator Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy profanity captions'; read the cmdlet's profanity and captions parameters, both caption-policy pages and Rooms/admin release notes. claims.claim: Teams admin center > Meetings > Meeting policies > policy > Live captions reaches the documented live-captions availability control.
claims.quote: go to Meetings > Meeting policies. Select the policy that you want to edit or create a new one. From the drop-down for Live captions, select Not enabled, but users can enable(default value) or Off.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity <policy name> -LiveCaptionsEnabledType Disabled turns off live captions for users with that policy.
claims.quote:
To turn off live captions for users with this policy, run the following script:
Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity <policy name> -LiveCaptionsEnabledType Disabled
